original_context_note: Compared /spec/full_target with the exact /full_target string in target-selection.json and problem.md:16–30: the full original target is preserved, including the approved nonemptiness condition, Euclidean product metric and n=0. H001 is precisely nonemptiness and H002 precisely compactness; H003 preserves n≥0 explicitly and is reported unused because the ambient natural-number index already represents exactly the original nonnegative integers. No proof conclusion is an H and no stronger condition was added. D001 defines the Euclidean metric by the finite squared-distance sum and fixes coordinate appending; D006 explicitly identifies the real line with Eucl(1) by t↦(t), retaining its exact metric, and D007 defines F=E×I. D002–D003 retain the supplied extended diameter, countable arbitrary-set covers, positive exponents, ≤δ scale convention, empty-set cost zero, infimum and supremum formulas with no normalizing factor. D004 names the actual native Hausdorff and dimH definitions read in the pinned sources; D005 and D008 do not assume finiteness. R001 proves their measure identification, rather than granting it as a definition. D009 names the canonical Lebesgue measure and nonnegative integral; none of these global operations has an unproved project construction guard. The partial constructions are local and guarded: R002/T follows F002, R003/J follows F001's finite endpoints, R004/N_i uses strictly positive r_i from its prior F002, R005/J_i follows F004, and R007/x0 follows H001. Successful probe_library evidence and actual source readbacks were inspected for M001–M017, including BorelSpace, NNReal, countability, measurability, bornology, open-cover, sign and boundedness conditions. M016 and M017 select the actual Real.exists_isLUB and Real.exists_isGLB declarations, not the earlier general discovery probes. The native Hausdorff formula, critical-exponent statements, integral-series equality, indicator integral, real interval measures, union bound, integral monotonicity, compactness consequences, power limits and real bounds are faithfully restated with their premises. The ordered book searches were unsuccessful and retained as access records; the book is only problem provenance, no E or unverified literature proposition is used, so there is no deferred-source assumption. The seven producers form the actual AND closure of P, and every selected M/N is used there; only H003 is unused. The original grid calculation, positive-diameter replacement, ceiling/product cost, slicing integration and epsilon/scale limits, interval dimension calculation and final two D cases are all retained. There is no material optional omission. This is same-author inspection under nl0-audit-a-8; structural validation and these notes do not claim independent Audit A acceptance.

output_notes.note: R001/S001 proves exact equality of the custom H^s with native measure at every positive exponent, including singleton/empty costs and elimination of radius ∞. S002 proves each of the four exported critical-exponent implications under that equality. S003 proves scale monotonicity, existence of arbitrarily cheap covers when H=0, and arbitrarily large contents at arbitrarily small scales when H=∞. All domains, quantifiers and normalization required by R002/R004/R006/R007 are present in /graph/propositions/@N001/statement.

R002/S001–S003 give the bounded box witness and finite ball-covers with finite cost for every positive s and δ, precisely the finiteness consumed by R005. S004 gives the explicit C h^(−n) cube count, √n h diameter and C n^(s/2)h^(s−n) zero-cost limit for s>n, and separately gives E=Eucl(0), D=0 using H001. The full 0≤D≤n and finiteness conclusion is exported, not left inside the producer.

R003/S001 supplies finite real least/greatest bounds from M016/M017 and derives sup B−inf B≤ρ. S002 constructs exactly the displayed J, proves containment, positivity/openness/boundedness and length≤ρ+η. The exported formula, nonemptiness/pairwise-distance premises, η>0 and allowance ρ=0 support both consumers without reading R003's body.

R004/S001 proves the n=0 conclusion and all q>D zero statements in F001. S002–S003 establish the positive-cover and product-cover estimates with exactly 2(√2)^(q+1)ε. S004 proves H^(q+1)_δ(F)=0 for every δ and H^(q+1)(F)=0 for every q>D; S005 obtains dim_H(F)≤D+1 using D finite from N002. Thus both the upper bound and the more precise exported clauses are proved.

R005/S001–S003 prove for every arbitrary admissible cover V and every ε>0 that c=H^s_δ(E)≤∑ρ_i^(s+1)+ε. S004 treats the infinite series case and, otherwise, removes ε with c finite; it then takes the infimum over all covers. The output is exactly H^s_δ(E)≤H^(s+1)_δ(F) for all s>0,δ>0, with no measurable-cover condition. This is the scale inequality actually consumed in R007.

R006/S001 supplies the interval upper bound. S002 proves ∑diam(U_i)≥1 for every countable δ-cover using interval enclosures and subadditivity. S003 proves H^s_δ(I)≥δ^(s−1), H^s(I)=∞ for 0<s<1 and dim_H(I)=1. S004 proves the full exported embedding comparison by explicitly pulling back arbitrary covers, including H^s_δ(I)≤H^s_δ(A) for every positive s,δ and dim_H(A)≥1. The consumer R007 receives the isometry conditions and full conclusion in the input statement.

R007/S001 proves the D>0 lower bound from the complete positive-scale inequality and critical exponents, retaining the supremum and s↑D argument. S002 proves the D=0 lower bound using x0∈E and the explicitly verified isometric map e(t)=(x0,t), including n=0. S003 combines the exhaustive cases (N002) and N004, then unfolds D,I,F to give precisely the full /spec/conclusion under the original hypotheses and Euclidean metric.
